independence_criteria: The reviewer is a distinct legal or natural person who is not the Owner and is not an entity the Owner controls, is employed by, or holds equity in.
The reviewer has no financial dependency on the Owner beyond the specific arm's-length review engagement itself.
The reviewer has no undisclosed pre-existing personal relationship with the Owner that could bias findings.
The reviewer was not granted repository write or admin access as part of or before the review.
The reviewer authored or selected their own review approach, prompts, and inputs rather than being handed a fixed script or a predetermined conclusion by the Owner.
The reviewer used their own compute, account, and infrastructure rather than Owner-provisioned or Owner-configured infrastructure.
The reviewer, not the Owner, selected and controlled which findings were submitted as the final review output.

Any payment, reciprocal consideration, or engagement benefit was structured as compensation for performing the review, never contingent on reaching a particular verdict or outcome — this covers unpaid or reciprocal arrangements (section 4.2, 4.4) exactly the same way it covers a paid one: the requirement is outcome-independence, not the presence of money. An arrangement with no consideration at all trivially satisfies this criterion.
The engagement and deliverable are bound to an authenticated External Evidence Provenance Record satisfying `docs/58` section 13 before independence can be claimed rather than merely asserted.

independence_disposition_rule.INDEPENDENT: all nine criteria verified true with evidence
independence_disposition_rule.UNKNOWN_INDEPENDENCE: any one criterion unverifiable or undocumented; default state before a real arrangement exists
precedence_order: NOT_INDEPENDENT if any criterion is verified false, regardless of the state of any other criterion
otherwise UNKNOWN_INDEPENDENCE if any criterion is unverifiable or undocumented
otherwise INDEPENDENT only if all nine are verified true with evidence

cardinality_proposal.reasoning_summary: one lane is a single point of failure; two lanes establish a cross-check floor; three lanes widen independent coverage (not a vote/tie-breaker -- every finding from any lane is still admitted and reconciled by Judge/Sergeant on its own merits per docs/58 section 1, evidence providers create facts not verdict votes); diversity across source classes guards against correlated blind spots; a larger N was rejected as unrealistic for a single-owner project with no evidenced dedicated assurance budget
